reading:
The judges love this lineage when the phosphor and the structure are the same thing. Lit Sill Line (8.00, feedback 8.8, soul 9.0, 6 promise votes) won because the greeting stands on its own Coming up rail. The breathing now lamp sends a lit run to the Next up tube, the tube's power lamp drops a lit wire onto the rail, airglow rises off the run, and Status types its lamps on scanlined glass. All of that is content lit where attention belongs, on grounded slate, with the family's things on ink plates. Branch Lines, Trued (7.91, the heat's best system) won on finish: named Status lamps on one instrument, the tube hung as tomorrow's stop, a numbered setup line ending at a buffer, To do's full-width lit NOW rule, and 'What's the plan?'.

What sank Lit Sill Line was structure and finish:
- The tube is read before the question.
- 'Coming up' sits under its own rail, after its plates.
- 'All plans' floats 40px off the buffer.
- Plate names wrap to two or three lines.
- Status lamps on the glass have no names, zero rows ('0 partly working · 0 stopped') add noise, and 160px of slate is dead beside the tally.
- The navy family plates read as an editor's selection, worst in Chat on a double rail.
- The month head says '2 coming' against the list's '5'.
- Row afterglow is invisible, and the phone's tube foot band is empty.

What sank Trued: the top of Home lost its phosphor, 'Or start with' looks like three more text fields, the short plates leave slate under the tall tube, the month folds to one lonely week, head figures are stacked in 12px beside the numeral, and the chat's Send is below the 900px fold.

Across the tour, the lessons say what wins:
- A refinement must move something on Home's first screen.
- A graft wins when it replaces something with data the page already holds, rebuilt in rails, buffers and 45-degree turns.
- No lamp may lie, so Status's 'This page' must be amber needs-a-look.
- Each count is said once.
- A page in time opens on now.
- The question is the largest head and is read first.

To win, the lineage keeps Lit Sill Line's light-as-structure and fixes the reading order, the station names and the buffers. It finishes Trued's instrument so the top of Home is lit again, and it grafts only devices that act on the lines themselves: the tick as the stop, quiet weeks as a dashed run, a one-line setup track and a single chat track.

briefs.name: Sill Line, Trued
briefs.hypothesis: Lit Sill Line already has the round's best feedback and soul. It lost 0.9-1.5 points on system, interaction, usability and type, and every one of those was a placement or finish fault on the first screen: the question read second, an orphaned head, a stranded link, wrapped plates, unnamed lamps and a selection-blue ink. Fixing exactly those, without touching the lit run, the wire or the airglow, should lift the lower lenses to about 8 while keeping soul at 9. That would make it the lineage's first design over 8.3.
briefs.brief:
Start from t2-track-graft (sheet.css, src/sill.css, templates). Keep its idea and mood.

HOME (templates/home.html, _ask.html, sill.css)
1. Question first. Re-lay .welcome.sill-board as two rows:
   (a) Vera's screen, name and day on one line, then the box full width across the board. 'What are we planning?' sits inside its frame as the h1 label, Archivo 700 at 2.5rem (clamp 1.9rem on phone), with 'planning' under E1's two layers. Send and the From row are under it. The ways to start sit under it as one row of three keys: #1b242b slate fill, no outline, 1px top highlight, 44px, sentence case.
   (b) The sill zone under the box. The now lamp breathes at the rail's left end. Above it, a station name plate stands on the rail: 'Coming up' (Archivo 600 1.25rem) with '5 coming · next tomorrow 10:00' on one line at 14px ink-2, baselines shared. The lit run goes from the now lamp to stop one, about 3rem. The Next up tube (.welcome .next-up, 22rem) stands ON the rail over stop one, and its power lamp drops the lit wire to the rail as now. Stops two to five run along the rest of the rail to a T buffer at the board's inner right edge. The buffer's own label is 'All plans →', set on the rail's line beside the bar, as setup's 'All the setup steps' is.
2. Stops and plates. Each stop's day stays in the glass zone above the rail: 30px Archivo 300 numeral, month over weekday 13px. Each plate hangs below on a 1px drop and takes 1fr of the remaining width. Set the name in the head face at 15px, text-wrap: balance, two lines at most. The foot line is pinned to the plate's bottom: '13:00' in mono, 'in 4 days' in DM Sans (the type fix).
3. Airglow. .welcome.sill-board::before still rises off the lit run only. E7's pool sits under Send at 0.13, and the box keeps its E4 resting halo. Nothing else on the board glows.
4. Ink. Warm the ink plate to #1a2230 with a #2a3646 edge. Give each plan plate a 2px #70dcf4 cyan cap (a plan is told at a glance), and drop the pale #86a9cc cap. Ink is used only for plans: Coming up, the Plans list and the month.
5. Calendar note. 'Google Calendar is not connected…' goes in ink-3 at 14px under the plates, left-aligned to stop two, not in the gutter.
6. Setup. Keep the line, the numbered hollow amber rings and the lit 'Next step' stop. Underline only the action phrase ('Choose your own password'); the rest of the clause is ink-2 and not linked. 'Next step' is set in sans at the label step, not mono.
7. To do. The margin timetable has the absolute date right-aligned in tabular figures ('Sun 27 Sep'), with 'was due 3 days ago' in amber beside it. The NOW rule runs the full row width as Trued's does, a 1px #6dff9c line with E21 bloom and 'now' in sage on the rail.
8. Lately added. A small cyan ring with 'Sun 4 Oct' marks an idea already on the calendar (from Trued).
9. Row afterglow on Home's rows, the plates, Ideas, To do and Settings. Pointing at or focusing a row lights a 2px #6dff9c left edge and a 10% green inner wash in .12s, fading over the kit's 1.2s curve (E9). It must be visible at 120 and 380ms.
10. Phone. Re-lay the tube's grid so the scope (4.5rem) sits beside the date and the foot band is gone: no empty glass above the prompt. Send shows its word.

STATUS (status.html)
- The glass keeps its scanlines, the three lamp rows and E20 breathing lamps. Under each lamp, its name in 11px VT323 dim strength on the glass (Chat, Digest, Lookups, Fallback; Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Telegram; Calendar, Weather, Web, Digest, This page).
- 'This page' is an amber half lamp, because Settings says Sign-in needs a look.
- Pull the tally into the same bezel, to the right of the glass, so no slate is left: '6 working · 1 waiting · 1 needs a look · 2 off · 4 not set up' as the big bone numerals stacked.
- Rows with zero are not drawn. 'Change the limit' goes under the tally.

CHAT (chat.html)
- Keep the double track and her glyph stops.
- The family's plates become neutral #161c20 slate with a 3px #86a9cc left bar. No navy in Chat.
- Only her newest stop is lit: screen halo, time in sage with soft bloom, bubble edge phosphor. Older edges are matte.
- Tighten the head (title 3rem, lede one line at 1280) so the composer and Send are on the first screen at 1280x900.

IDEAS (ideas.html)
- Drive figures are bold with light units ('2 h 10 min'), right-aligned so 'min' stacks. A separate Way column holds S, SE and so on.
- Use 'No.' as the head with bare numerals, no '#'.
- Lighting a stop on the line from home works on :focus-within and on tap, as well as hover.
- Name the nearest and furthest above the line, as now.

PLANS
- Month (plans_month.html): open on the week holding today. The past weeks fold to one 32px strip, '31 Aug – 27 Sep · nothing on', with a dashed steel run. The lit run stays on today's week.
- The head says one count, and only what the month shows ('2 more this month · next tomorrow 10:00'). It never puts a second figure beside the list's.
- List (plans.html): each plan's name on an ink plate with the cyan cap.

TO DO, SETTINGS, FORM
- To do page: the full-width NOW rule; quiet text 'Edit' (44px hit area, no box).
- Settings: the lamp column keeps its states. Sign-in gets the amber half lamp with 'Needs a look' as now.
- Form (idea_form.html): a 2px rail down the label edge with a stop at each field. The focused field's stop lights #6dff9c with E21. 'Everything else' gets its own stop. Required fields are marked 'needed' in amber words. Selects get the same 2px #6dff9c focus ring as fields.

Update the palette's companions note and decisions to match.

briefs.title: What are *planning*? is kept as 'What are we *planning*?'. It is the lineage's highest-scoring title (8.00, best for feedback, soul and style on this design), because the lit line of plans directly under the box answers it. It is the household's present tense, inviting them to tell Vera what is on the go. The system and type lenses' worry was length and wrapping. With the box now across the board's full width it holds one line at 40px on desktop and about 29px on a phone, and the eight lit letters are the page's one hot word, since NEXT UP stays in the tube's inverse plate.

briefs.name: Trued, Relit
briefs.hypothesis: Trued had the heat's best system (7.5) and the best sight line, with the tube as tomorrow's stop and Status as one named instrument. It lost because its first screen went dark and its ways to start read as fields. Putting the phosphor back on the greeting in its own way (lit glass behind the box and a lit branch line of starters), filling the plates to the tube's height, and opening the month on now should move every lens that faulted the top of Home. Its structure stays distinct from Lit Sill Line: two boards, with the tube hanging below the rail.
briefs.brief:
Start from t2-track-refine (sheet.css, src/trued.css, templates). Keep its idea: the tube is the main line's first lamp, hung below Coming up's rail like every other plate, and the greeting is its own board.

HOME GREETING (home.html, _ask.html, trued.css)
1. Light the top again.
   - E7 goes back behind the box: a radial pool from the lower left under Send at about 0.16, with the kit's masked scanlines (2px period, 6%) inside the board only.
   - The box gets E4's resting halo (0 0 0 1px brand at 35%, 0 0 28px -6px brand at 25%), stronger on :focus-within. The frame lights #6dff9c on focus.
   - 'plan' takes E1's full two layers, so it is brighter than Send's pool.
   - Vera's screen beside her name breathes (E19 glyph halo).
2. Ways to start as a branch line. The three outlined boxes go.
   - A 2px steel branch leaves the box's right edge at the From row's height, turns down with one 45-degree chamfer, and runs down the right column.
   - 'Or start with' is the station name at the junction (14px ink-2, cap height on the branch).
   - Three stops follow. Each is a 12px steel ring joined by a short spur to its key: #1b242b slate fill, no border, 1px top highlight, 44px tall, left-aligned words, a trailing → in steel.
   - The branch ends at a T buffer.
   - When the box has focus, the junction ring lights #6dff9c with E21, so the stop you are at lights while you write.
   - Phone: the keys stack under the box with the branch down their left edge.

COMING UP (the board under the greeting)
3. Head on one line. 'Coming up', then '5 coming · next tomorrow 10:00' at 15px ink-2, its first baseline on the head's baseline. No stacked 12px labels. Apply the same rule to every page head's figure ('12 ideas · 10 on the line', '4 open · 2 late', '5 coming · next tomorrow 10:00'), one line, and on the phone under the head.
4. Plates fill the tube's height. Tube at 20rem, plates 1fr each. Each plate holds:
   - a kind ring in its grounded colour, and who it is for at 14px ink-2;
   - the name in the head face at 15px, balanced, two lines at most;
   - at its foot a sunk readout well (#080c0d, inset 0 1px 4px #000 at .85, mono tabular) holding '13:00', with 'in 4 days' in sans beside it.
   Each plate's foot aligns with the tube's foot.
   The family's plates are #1b2531 with a 2px cyan #74e6f0 cap (they are plans).
5. The tube. Its '›▮' line becomes the link '› 4 more on the line▮' with a blinking cursor. Keep E16 power-on, at 0.1s warm-up.

STILL ON HOME
6. Setup: keep the numbered stations and buffer. Set 'Next step' in sans at the label step, and underline only the action words.
7. To do (Home and page): the margin DUE timetable comes back, with the absolute date right-aligned and tabular ('Sun 27 Sep 19:56'), and the relative words amber in the When column. The boxed Edit keys become a quiet text 'Edit' with a 44px target. The full-width NOW rule stays.

STATUS
- Keep the instrument and the legend.
- 'This page' becomes an amber half lamp. The tally reads '6 working · 1 waiting · 1 needs a look · 2 off · 4 not set up'.
- Status's 'live' becomes 'working' everywhere.

PLANS
- Month: never open on one lonely week. Today's week and the rest of the month show in full. The past weeks fold to one 32px dashed-steel strip, '31 Aug – 27 Sep · nothing on'.
- Under the last week, the rail runs on past the grid's edge to a T buffer labelled 'October continues · Later →', the pager's own link, so the drawing carries past the month.
- Weekend columns (Sat, Sun, heads included) are one 2-3 dE slate step lighter.
- The head says '5 coming' only if the month's context has the list's count; otherwise it says what the grid holds ('2 more in September').

IDEAS
- Move 'the line from home' below the table, or into a disclosure ('Show the line from home'), so the list is on the first screen.
- Print 'Nearest: Pumpkin patch, 18 min' and 'Furthest: Cannon Beach, 2 h 45' as text above the line, so no label collides with the ticks.
- A stop on the line lights on the row's :focus-within as well as hover.

CHAT
- At 1280x900 the composer must show From and Send on the first screen. Shorten the head (title 3rem, a one-line lede) and reduce the date strip's margins.
- Only her newest stop is lit, as now. The family plates keep the #9cc3dd bar on #1b2531.

AFTERGLOW
Replace every steel or sage row wash with a 2px #6dff9c left edge and a 10% wash, in at .12s and out over 1.2s (E9). Apply it to the plates, Ideas rows, To do rows and Settings rows.

FORM AND SETTINGS
- Selects get the same 2px #6dff9c focus ring as fields.
- The form keeps its label rail and required markers, and gets one stop inside 'Everything else'.

PHONE
Send shows the word. The head figure sits on one line under the head.

briefs.title: 'What's the *plan*?' is kept: Trued's own title, which the skeptic ranked first, system and usability joint first, and seven notes in round 1 favoured. It is the kitchen-table phrase, 16 characters, one line at 40px anywhere, and it lights the job word at the line's end where the eye stops. Here the lit branch of starters beside it reads as the answers to 'the plan'. Nothing else on the screen glows 'plan', and the tube's inverse NEXT UP keeps a different word.

briefs.name: Sill Line, Ticked
briefs.hypothesis: Lit Sill Line's light is already the tour's best. What it lacks is a set of grafts that make the lines do work: the stop on To do becomes the tick you press, quiet weeks become a dashed run instead of empty grid, setup becomes a one-line track so the week and To do rise up the first screen, and Chat gets one track with branch ticks instead of a navy double rail. Each device replaces something rather than adding beside it, which is the lessons' test for a graft that takes. With the question lifted to head the whole board, it fixes the reading order while keeping the original tube-beside-box composition, so it differs from both refinements at a thumbnail.
briefs.brief:
Start from t2-track-graft (Lit Sill Line).

HOME GREETING (home.html, _ask.html, sill.css)
- The board opens on a full-width headline row: Vera's screen and name small at the left, then the question as the h1 <label for="text">, 'What needs planning?', in Archivo 700 at 2.75rem (clamp 2rem on a phone), 'planning' in E1's two layers. It is the largest head on Home and the first thing read.
- Under it, Lit Sill Line's composition stays: the Next up tube (22rem) at the left standing on the sill, and the textarea, From and Send at the right with E4's resting halo. Their tops share one line.
- Ways to start: one row under the box of three #1b242b slate keys, no outline, 44px.
- The sill keeps the breathing now lamp, the lit run to stop one, the power lamp's wire and the airglow.
- 'Coming up · 5 coming' becomes a station plate set IN a break of the rail between the now lamp and stop one: the rail stops 8px either side of it, as a legend sits in a demarcation break, on the rail's centre line. It is no longer under the rail.
- 'All plans →' is the T buffer's label at the rail's right end.
- Plate names are balanced, two lines at most. Ink is warmed to #1a2230 with a 2px #70dcf4 cap, and used only for plans.

GRAFT 1, setup cut to one line (L042). The 210px 'Finish setting up' board becomes one strip between the greeting and To do, about 56px:
- an amber outline triangle and 'Finish setting up' (Archivo 600 1rem);
- a short steel track of three hollow amber rings numbered 1-3, the first with a #6dff9c rim and E21 halo;
- the next step as the one link, 'Next: choose your own password →';
- 'All 3 steps' as the T buffer's label at the track's end.
The strip has an amber 1px left edge on slate #161c20. Phone: two lines (the track and the link).

GRAFT 2, the tick is the stop (L048 with L255's state), on Home's To do and the To do page (tasks.html). The rail's node and the checkbox become one control. The separate checkbox column goes, and each row reads: date margin | stop | task | who | Edit.
- The control (the finish_task button or checkbox, whatever the template uses) is a transparent 2.75rem hit square centred on the rail line with negative margins, so the row's rhythm does not move.
- ::before draws the stop as a 1.15rem ring:
  - steel #7d8fa0 when open;
  - amber #ffb850 2px when late, with 'was due 3 days ago' amber in the margin;
  - dashed pewter with no date;
  - sage #86d9a6 filled, with a clip-path tick in ::after, once done. It flashes the kit's tight halo on press, then fades over --afterglow.
- Focus: a 2px #6dff9c ring inset .55rem round the drawn ring.
- The full-width lit NOW rule crosses at its place, as Trued's does.
- Margin: the absolute date right-aligned and tabular ('Sun 27 Sep'), with the relative words in amber beside it.
- 'Edit' is quiet text with a 44px target.

GRAFT 3, quiet weeks as a dashed run (L122, with L132's weekend columns), on Plans > Month (plans_month.html) and the Plans list:
- A run of past or empty weeks folds to one 32px row: a dashed steel line between two small hollow lamps, labelled '31 Aug – 27 Sep · nothing on' in 14px ink-2, tabular.
- Today's week never folds and carries the lit run from 'now' to the next plan.
- Sat and Sun columns, heads included, are one 2-3 dE slate step lighter.
- Under the grid the rail runs on to a T buffer labelled 'October continues · Later →'.
- The head says one count, of what is shown.
- On the Plans list, a gap of a week or more between plans is the same dashed run with 'nothing on'.

GRAFT 4, one chat track with branch ticks (L209), in chat.html. The double rail goes.
- From 40rem, one 2px steel track drops from Vera's screen tile down a left gutter. The times hang in a right-aligned tabular margin left of it: the same timetable rule as To do's margin.
- Her replies hang from her glyph stop on the track in her matte bubble. Only her newest stop is lit (screen halo, time in sage with bloom, bubble edge phosphor).
- Each family message gets a 12px steel ring on the track and a 1px pewter tick running across to its bubble at the right: neutral #161c20 slate with a 3px #86a9cc left bar and the name in steel. No navy.
- The track ends in a #6dff9c ring with E21 halo and 'your turn', with a tick to the composer.
- The head is tightened so the composer's Send is on the first screen at 1280x900.
- Below 40rem the track hides and the bubbles take the width.

STATUS
- Names under each lamp on the glass in 11px VT323 dim.
- 'This page' becomes an amber half lamp, with 'needs a look 1' in the tally.
- The tally sits beside the glass in one bezel, and zero rows are not drawn.

IDEAS
- A Way column, right-aligned drive with bold figures.
- The line from home's stop lights on row focus and on tap.

SETTINGS AND FORM
- The settings list rows get the phosphor edge afterglow.
- The form gets a label rail whose stop lights on the focused field, and selects get the 2px focus ring.

AFTERGLOW EVERYWHERE
Rows light a 2px #6dff9c edge and a 10% wash, fading over 1.2s.

PHONE
- The headline question is first, then the box, then the tube on the vertical rail with the foot band trimmed.
- Send shows its word.
- The setup strip is two lines.

- 'The tube is read before the question' and ''Coming up' orphaned under its rail' (all lenses).
- 'All plans floats off the buffer' and 'unnamed Status lamps'.
- 'Zero rows' and 'the lamp that lies'.
- 'Mouse-only lighting', and 'the whole setup clause underlined', which goes because the setup is now one link.
- 'The lower half is the parent's' (style), since To do's rows are rebuilt with tick-stops.

It keeps the lineage recognisable: rails, rings, T buffers, a lit run from now, and the tube standing on the sill. It imports no main-line structure.
briefs.title:
'What needs *planning*?' is new, never tried in the tour. It invites the family to tell Vera anything that wants arranging, which is the whole job: a weekend, an idea to keep, a reminder, a calendar entry, a wish. It avoids the judges' objections to the favourites:
- It cannot be answered 'no' as 'Anything to plan?' can.
- It does not presume a plan exists, as 'What's the plan?' and 'What's our plan?' were faulted for.
- It is not an order, as 'Tell Vera what to plan.' was called.
- It is not a status check, as the -ing of 'What are we planning?' was heard.
Its lit word is the job and ends the line where the eye stops. At 20 characters, set as the board's full-width headline, it holds one line at 2.75rem on desktop and about 2rem on a phone. It differs from both refinements' titles, so the judges can compare three.
